passage.text_en:
Long before paper existed, people wrote on materials such as clay, stone, and animal skins. These materials worked, but they had clear drawbacks. Clay tablets were heavy and could break, while animal skins were expensive and slow to prepare. As societies grew and needed to record more information, a lighter and cheaper writing surface became necessary.

The solution appeared in ancient China around two thousand years ago. Workers learned to soak plant fibers in water, beat them into a soft pulp, and spread the mixture thinly across a flat screen. When the water drained and the layer dried, it formed a smooth sheet of paper. The process was simple enough to repeat many times, so paper could be produced in large amounts.

This new material spread slowly along trade routes, reaching other regions over several centuries. Wherever it arrived, paper made writing easier and books more affordable. By lowering the cost of recording ideas, paper helped knowledge travel farther than ever before.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Clay tablets were the best writing material ever made.
options.B: Paper was invented to meet the need for a lighter, cheaper writing surface, and it spread widely.
options.C: Ancient China was the largest country in the world.
options.D: Animal skins are still used for writing today.

questions.explanation_ar: النص يشرح مشكلة المواد القديمة، ثم اختراع الورق كحلّ أخفّ وأرخص، ثم انتشاره. هذا هو الموضوع العام.
questions.avoid_tip_ar: الفكرة الرئيسية تجمع كل الفقرات. تجنّب الخيارات الجزئية (الألواح الطينية) أو خارج الموضوع (حجم الصين).

questions.q: According to the passage, what was a problem with animal skins?
questions.q_translation_ar: حسب النص، ما المشكلة في جلود الحيوانات؟

options.A: They were too light to write on.
options.B: They were expensive and slow to prepare.
options.D: They were only found in China.

questions.explanation_ar: الفقرة الأولى تذكر صراحة أن الجلود كانت غالية وبطيئة التحضير.
questions.avoid_tip_ar: عُد للسبب المذكور حرفياً. باقي الخيارات لم تُذكَر في النص إطلاقاً.

questions.q: The word 'pulp' in the passage is closest in meaning to:
questions.q_translation_ar: كلمة 'pulp' في النص أقرب معنىً إلى:
questions.explanation_ar: pulp تعني (عجينة/لبّ): الألياف تُضرَب لتصير مزيجاً ليّناً رطباً قبل فرده.
questions.avoid_tip_ar: السياق يقول إنها تُضرَب في الماء وتُفرَد، فهي رطبة ليّنة لا صلبة ولا جافة.

questions.q: Why does the author describe the papermaking process in the second paragraph?
questions.q_translation_ar: لماذا يصف الكاتب عملية صناعة الورق في الفقرة الثانية؟

options.A: To prove that paper was difficult and rarely made.
options.B: To show how a simple, repeatable process allowed paper to be produced in large amounts.
options.D: To explain how clay tablets were made.

questions.explanation_ar: وصف العملية يوضّح أنها بسيطة وقابلة للتكرار، ولذلك أمكن إنتاج الورق بكميات كبيرة — وهذا غرض الفقرة.
questions.avoid_tip_ar: أسئلة الغرض تسأل (لماذا ذُكر هذا؟). النص يصف العملية ليبيّن سهولتها، لا لينتقد العمال.

questions.q: What can be inferred about the spread of paper?
questions.q_translation_ar: ماذا يمكن استنتاجه عن انتشار الورق؟

options.A: It happened instantly all over the world.
options.B: It took a long time and followed trade connections between regions.
options.C: It was kept secret and never left China.
options.D: It made books more expensive everywhere.

questions.explanation_ar: النص يقول إن الورق انتشر ببطء عبر طرق التجارة على مدى قرون، فنستنتج أن انتشاره كان تدريجياً ومرتبطاً بالتجارة.
questions.avoid_tip_ar: تجنّب المتطرّف (فوراً / لم يغادر الصين). والنص يقول إن الورق جعل الكتب أرخص لا أغلى.
